title: World Cup winner odds put France as clear favorite ahead of Spain, England, Argentina
text:
World Cup Odds

After storming through the competition, France is the clear favorite to win the 2026 World Cup. Kevin C. Cox / Getty Images

The World Cup quarterfinals featured meetings of former champions against potential first-time winners. In all four quarterfinals, the former champion won. The result is a competitive and mostly balanced final four, but one team still remains the clear favorite.

France has top-dog status in the sportsbooks with +140 odds on FanDuel and +150 odds on DraftKings and BetMGM. Les Bleus have an attack that has looked nearly unstoppable and have had the most stress-free journey to the semifinals. France has been the tournament favorite since the first set of group matches finished.

Advertisement

The French are the only team to win every match in group play and all three knockout matches within 90 minutes. Only one game has been remotely close: a 1-0 victory against Paraguay in the final 16. Even in that match, Opta didn’t credit Paraguay with a shot on target. The only way it appeared close was in the final score.

The rest of the remaining field is full of traditional powers in the sport, but none are being given the same respect France is. Spain, England and Argentina are all a solid amount behind France in the odds, but are tightly bunched among themselves.

Spain has odds between +320 and +333 on the three sportsbooks mentioned above, but England is actually ahead of La Roja on FanDuel. There, England is +310 and Spain is +330. That is a bit of an outlier, but the two are incredibly close wherever you look. Argentina has settled in as the relative long shot of the group, but even then, La Albiceleste are no longer than +400 (4-to-1) anywhere, and are typically shorter than that.


With those odds, France would be clearly favored in the final against either team, but Spain would also likely be favored against England or Argentina. Spain’s odds are currently longer because of the upcoming meeting with France, the unanimous top-rated team in the tournament. If Spain were to defeat France, it would emerge as the favorite in the final unless there is a significant injury or suspension.

It’s interesting that for as talked about as France has been, Les Bleus are still not favored against the whole field. At +150 odds, France is only being given a roughly 40 percent chance of winning the World Cup. So while France is clearly more likely than any of the other remaining teams individually, it is currently viewed as more likely that France will not win the World Cup than it will.

Even though France has done nothing to lose its spot as the most impressive team for the last month, every team has a decent chance of winning against the other. The French attack has looked so good so far that it seems hard to believe Les Bleus could lose, but every team left is loaded with talent.

Both semifinal matches are incredibly tight in the odds as well. No team is favored to win inside 90 minutes. Picking anyone to win in regulation is currently plus-money. France is a bigger favorite against Spain, with implied odds around 60 percent to advance, while England is a small favorite against Argentina.

This group of semifinalists guarantees there won’t be a new World Cup winner. Only eight countries (the four still playing plus Italy, Brazil, Uruguay and Germany) have won World Cups, and that will still be true entering 2030. That also means Europe and South America will still hold all the titles. One trend could be broken, though. England’s Thomas Tuchel has a chance to be the first manager to win a men’s World Cup who wasn’t born in the country of the team he managed.
